newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FCNZ year profit includes extraordinary payment.
newsitem.headline: FCNZ year profit includes extraordinary payment.

text.p: Forestry Corp of New Zealand on Tuesday released its annual report showing an after-tax profit of NZ$167.9 million in the year to June 30 against a previous 15 month profit of $141.2 million.
The goverment last week announced it had sold FCNZ to a consortium of Fletcher Challenge Forest Division, Brierley Investments Ltd and China's Citifor, a unit of Citic, for a net $1.6 billion.

The profit includes an extraordinary back payment of $110 million, $74 million after tax, from Fletcher Challenge relating to the resolution of FCNZ's long-term log supply contract with Fletcher subdiary Tasman.
It relates to wood supplied by the corporation to Fletcher Challenge betwween 1990-5 and was the result of an arbitration agreement in February 1995. It was paid at the end of 1995.
Shareholders' funds were in the report at $1.6 billion against $1.79 billion previously while the forests were valued at $1.85 billion against $2.12 billion previously.
FCNZ's trading result excluding the back payment was $94.2 million, against the budgeted figure of $82.2 million.
FCNZ paid the government a dividend in March of $100 million, more than 25 percent over budget.
The result represented a return on equity of 12.8 percent against a target of 12.1 percent. The return on assets was 10.2 percent against a target of 9.9 percent.
Gross revenues were $501 million including the back payment against $495.2 million previously.
Chairman Rosanne Meo said the profit came despite tough international market conditions for wood and many products made from wood fibre.
The corporation still needed multi-million dollar investment in improving facilities for further downstream processing of wood and improving distribution chains.
She said privatisation of FCNZ was a necessity.

Meo said the backpayment signalled the realisation of one of FCNZ's major goals since its existence -- satisfactory resolution and clarification of its long-term wood supply contract with Fletcher unit, Tasman Pulp and Paper.
Chief executive Tim Cullinane said that since 1991 FCNZ had returned over $1.25 billion to the government in dividends, loan and capital repayments and tax.
